ideas.description: Exploit E014. Port the E014 Muon optimizer exactly as it was onto the tip E010 commit (5aa9aa5: LS 0.2, cudnn.benchmark, max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, F.max_pool2d head). Muon settings: conv filters except the frozen whitening conv, Nesterov momentum 0.6, lr 0.24, 5 quintic NS steps in bf16, update scaled by sqrt(max(1,out/in)) on the flattened [out,in*k*k] matrix. BN biases and the head stay on the existing SGD, and lookahead is kept. Make ONE recipe change: epochs 9 -> 8, with the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules scaled to the new step count. The final partial batch shape is compiled in build(). Before launching, run the one-step finite-gradient check (drafts/debug_nan.py), because the compiled NS and Muon graph is new to the tip's compile mode. Log the optimizer step time separately.
ideas.expected: New best. Accuracy 0.756-0.764 (point ~0.760): E014's +1.3 pp at 9 epochs minus ~0.8-1.2 pp for one fewer epoch. Time 7.75-8.10 s (point ~7.95 s): tip per-epoch ~0.89 s plus ~0.09 s/epoch Muon overhead measured in E014, times 8 epochs. Below 0.753 would mean Muon's gain collapses at shorter horizons; then retry at 8.5 epochs.

ideas.description: Cut Muon's per-step overhead. E014 added ~10% time, or ~1.9 ms/step, for NS. Take the Muon 8-epoch recipe above and change only the Newton-Schulz iteration count from 5 to 3 quintic steps, keeping the same coefficients (airbench94_muon uses 3; D002 C0013-C0015 show final quality is insensitive to exact orthogonalization). Keep everything else identical. Report the optimizer step time per step against the 5-step run.
ideas.expected: Time 3-5% lower than the 5-step Muon run at the same epoch count (~7.6-7.75 s if that run lands at ~7.95 s). Accuracy within +-0.25 pp of the 5-step run, which is re-draw noise. A drop >0.3 pp means the larger late-block matrices need the full 5 steps; then try 3 steps only on the 128-wide block-1 filters.

ideas.description: Find the Muon knee below 8 epochs. Run this after the Muon 8-epoch run, and only if it scores >=0.758. Take the better of the 5-step and 3-step NS variants and change only the epoch count, from 8 to 7.5. Scale all schedules to the step count. The last half-epoch uses the first half of that epoch's permutation, as in E006.
ideas.expected: Accuracy 0.751-0.759 (point ~0.755). Time ~7.3-7.5 s, about 8-10% below the tip. If it is feasible, it reaches H1.2.1's <=7.3 s target region. If it is infeasible by <0.3 pp, combine it with the lr or averaging tuning below rather than trimming further.

ideas.description: Tune Muon's lr, which was inherited untuned from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon. On the Muon 8-epoch recipe (or 7.5 epochs if that becomes the tip), change only the Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.36. The SGD lr for BN biases and the head stays the same. If it falls by more than 0.25 pp, the follow-up direction is 0.16.
ideas.expected: Accuracy moves by +-0.2-0.5 pp at unchanged time. A gain >=0.25 pp buys ~0.25-0.5 epoch of slack, worth ~3-5% time at the knee. Most likely the effect is within noise (lr 0.24 already near optimal); that settles the lr axis.

ideas.description: Test whether Muon's update normalization replaces averaging. On the Muon 8-epoch recipe, remove lookahead (plain Muon + Nesterov SGD, no weight averaging) and change nothing else. Compare it paired against the Muon 8-epoch run with lookahead. This is purely informative about the H4.2/H1.2 interaction: it decides whether averaging tuning (H1.6) is still worth runs on the Muon base.
ideas.expected: Accuracy 0.5-1.2 pp lower than Muon with lookahead (most likely infeasible). Time ~0.5-1% lower, saving the lookahead blend of ~0.06 s. A drop <=0.25 pp would refute H1.2.2 and make lookahead removable, with averaging work moving to EMA.

ideas.description: Systems change that transfers to any recipe. On the current tip (the Muon successor if one is kept, else E010), replace GELU with SiLU everywhere and change nothing else. SiLU's sigmoid is cheaper than GELU's erf, and Inductor may fuse its BN+act backward with less recompute. Run the one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first (E009 lesson), and re-profile the Triton elementwise share.
ideas.expected: Time -0.5% to -2.5%: the elementwise kernels are memory-bound, so the gain is mostly lost compute and smaller than H2.4.1's >=3%. Accuracy within +-0.25 pp. A time change under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1; if so, retire this lever.

ideas.description: Combine near-misses. E013's progressive resizing saved 13.9% time but cost 0.8 pp, which was infeasible on the SGD tip with 0.2 pp of margin. Muon's extra accuracy may absorb that cost. On the Muon 8-epoch recipe, run only the first 2 epochs (25%) on 24 px random crops, with the rest at 32 px. Compile both resolutions in build(). Nothing else changes.
ideas.expected: Time ~8-9% below the Muon 8-epoch run (a 24 px epoch costs ~59% of a 32 px one, and NS cost per step is unchanged). Accuracy ~0.4-0.6 pp lower. It wins only if it beats the Muon epoch trade-off (~0.18 pp per 1% time); the likely outcome is roughly break-even, which would confirm low-res epochs as a worse trade than fewer epochs.

drop.reason: Proxy-based batch selection (H1.4.1, confidence 0.15) is expected to come out neutral or worse at ~9 epochs: it adds 8-15% proxy overhead for an uncertain gain. Muon (E014: +1.3 pp at 9 epochs) is a much cheaper source of sample efficiency, so this has the lowest expected value in the queue.

It is specified on the SGD tip (E007), which is about to be superseded by a Muon recipe. Capacity and FLOP exchange rates measured on SGD won't transfer. Rebase it on the Muon knee once that is found.

structured_output.summary: E014 is the main signal. Muon on the conv filters, with lookahead kept, gave 0.7681 at 9 epochs, +1.3 pp over the SGD recipe, at ~10% NS overhead. That is worth about 2 epochs, so the queue now focuses on cashing it in. The top priority is Muon ported onto the E010 tip at 8 epochs (expected ~0.760 in ~7.95 s, a new best). Next, cut the NS overhead to 3 steps, then push the knee to 7.5 epochs (~7.4 s, toward H1.2.1's 7.3 s target). After that, one Muon lr probe. The explore third: test whether Muon makes lookahead redundant (H1.2.2), try a SiLU swap as a transferable systems cut (H2.4.1), and combine E013's progressive resizing with Muon's slack. I dropped I013 (low expected value next to Muon) and I017 (specified on an SGD tip that is being superseded; rebase it later). Decisions follow the noise rule: accuracy deltas under 0.25 pp and time deltas under 1.5% count as inconclusive.
